fixes.explanation: Pharaoh is a fair guess since Egypt shows up later in this passage. But Isaiah says the remnant "…will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel." (Isaiah 10:20). Egypt comes up only as a memory of earlier days (Isaiah 10:24, 26). Leaning on Pharaoh is not the plan.

Nebuchadnezzar was a king of Babylon (Jeremiah 27:6), but he isn't in this passage at all. Isaiah says the remnant "…will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel." (Isaiah 10:20). No king gets that spot. Friend, I'd have mixed up the kings too before my first batch of the day.

Nobody counts sand at the beach, it just goes on and on. Isaiah says "Though your people, O Israel, be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return." (Isaiah 10:22). So the picture is a crowd too big to count. And then comes the surprising turn.
You got it, baker! Isaiah says "…the Lord GOD of Hosts will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land." (Isaiah 10:23). This is a heavy verse. The word that matters is whole.

Walls aren't mentioned here at all, friend. Isaiah says "…the Lord GOD of Hosts will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land." (Isaiah 10:23). That's the whole land, not one piece of it. It's a heavy verse.

You got it, baker! Isaiah says, "The yoke will be broken because your neck will be too large." (Isaiah 10:27). A yoke sits on the neck, so a neck too big snaps it right off. The burden comes off the shoulders and the yoke off the neck.

You got it, baker! Isaiah says, "Yet today they will halt at Nob, shaking a fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem." (Isaiah 10:32). After all those towns, the march halts at Nob. Then comes the fist, and I can feel the tension.

You got it, baker! The fist shakes "…at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem." (Isaiah 10:32). Zion and Jerusalem are the same hill in that line. All those towns fleeing, and then comes the fist at Jerusalem's hill.

Samaria is a fair guess, but Isaiah doesn't name it here. He says the fist shakes "…at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem." (Isaiah 10:32). Jerusalem is the target. It's the hill the fist is shaken at.
Damascus isn't in this passage, friend. Isaiah says the fist shakes "…at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem." (Isaiah 10:32). That hill is the target. Different map, but a good try.

You got it, baker! Isaiah says, "The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled." (Isaiah 10:33). The Lord lops off the branches with terrifying power, and the tall trees come down. The picture shifts from a marching army to a forest.

Not quite, friend. Isaiah says the opposite: "…Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One." (Isaiah 10:34). Here Lebanon falls, it doesn't stand firm. The line comes right after He clears the forest thickets with an axe.

You got it, baker! Isaiah says, "…Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One." (Isaiah 10:34). It comes after the axe clears the forest thickets. Lebanon doesn't stand firm, it falls before the Mighty One.
